messages.subject: WBIC in rstan
parts:
Dear all

Now I try to calculate WBIC (Widely applicable Bayesian Information Criterion) from the result of rstan. WBIC is the average log likelihood function over the posterior distribution with the inverse temperature 1/log(n). So, I try to write a stan code in wbic_test.stan. R script is written in wbic_test.r. The result is as follows:


Inference for Stan model: wbic_test.
4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1;
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff
beta[1] 0.89 0.01 0.48 -0.03 0.63 0.90 1.16 1.82 1451
beta[2] 2.18 0.01 0.52 1.23 1.90 2.17 2.45 3.22 1444
sigma 1.14 0.02 0.58 0.54 0.79 1.00 1.31 2.66 783
loglik -27.89 0.21 5.65 -42.03 -30.56 -26.48 -23.72 -21.34 703
lp__ -9.27 0.06 1.59 -13.38 -9.99 -8.85 -8.11 -7.44 733
Rhat
beta[1] 1.00
beta[2] 1.01
sigma 1.00
loglik 1.00
lp__ 1.00


However, the result is not so good, especially sd of parameters. If I run normally written stan code (wbic_test_2.stan), the result is good as follows:


Inference for Stan model: wbic_test_2.
4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1;
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff
beta[1] 0.91 0.00 0.18 0.57 0.79 0.91 1.03 1.25 1989
beta[2] 2.16 0.00 0.19 1.79 2.03 2.16 2.28 2.52 1986
sigma 0.78 0.00 0.14 0.56 0.68 0.76 0.86 1.10 1927
loglik -22.57 0.04 1.38 -26.08 -23.23 -22.23 -21.56 -20.99 1210
lp__ -4.46 0.04 1.30 -7.75 -5.09 -4.12 -3.51 -2.97 1229
Rhat
beta[1] 1
beta[2] 1
sigma 1
loglik 1
lp__ 1


If I have problems, please let me know. Or, if I don’t have any problems, do you have any idea how to improve this result? I use rstan 2.6.0 in R 3.1.2 on Mac OS X 10.10.2.

The explanation of WBIC is here: Watanabe, S. 2013. A widely applicable Bayesian information criterion. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 14 (Mar), 867-897.

Sincerely,

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Kiwamu Ishikura

messages.subject: Re: WBIC in rstan
parts:
I did WBIC for more complicated model and I recommend to use WAIC unless you know what you are doing.

Any way, here is my comment. 
sd estimated by a model with inverse temperature (wbic_test.stan) is not the same as sd estimated by a model without inverse temperature (wbic_test_2.stan).
the results from wbic_test.stan and wbic_test_2.stan never be the same!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] WBIC in rstan
parts:
These are fundamentally different models.

Your programs have the same data, transformed data, and
paramters:

data {
int N;
vector[N] x;
vector[N] y;
}
transformed data {
matrix[N,2] X;
real Nr;

Nr <- N;
for (n in 1:N) {
X[n,1] <- 1.0;
X[n,2] <- x[n];
}
}
parameters {
vector[2] beta;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}


The difference is in the log density function:


wbic_test.stan
------------------------------
model {
increment_log_prob(1/log(Nr) * normal_log(y, X * beta, sigma));
}


wbic_test_2.stan
-----------------------
model {
y ~ normal(X * beta, sigma);
}


If you look at the log densities (up to an additive constant)
in the two programs, you have:


test.stan:

1/log(Nr) * (-log(sigma) - 0.5 * ((y - X * beta) / sigma)^2

test_2.stan:

-log(sigma) - 0.5 * ((y - X * beta) / sigma)^2


Because the posterior density is proportional to these, it
varies between the two models.

- Bob
